did.abstract: The collection comprises correspondence, articles, cuttings, and other related material, concerning the English antiquary and topographer, John Britton (1771-1857).

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection comprises correspondence, articles, cuttings, and other related material, concerning the English antiquary and topographer, John Britton (1771-1857). It includes correspondence with Joseph Hume on the preservation of British antiquities. Also present is material related to Britton's various published works on architectural antiquities, including correspondence with the artist George Cattermole.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection is arranged into the following series: Series 1. Correspondence (1805-1852), Series 2. Printed Material (1820-1855), Series 3. Publications (1815-1830), Series 4. Additional material (1789-1845).

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: John Britton was a prolific topographer, writer, and editor in the early nineteenth century. Britton was born 1 July 1771 in Wiltshire, England, to Henry Britton and Anne Hillier. John was one of ten children. Britton became interested in topography in 1789 following a meeting with his future collaborator Edward Wedlake Brayley. Together, they worked with the publisher Vernon and Hood to undertake a topographical survey of England and Wales. Brayley and Britton traveled primarily on foot, and the extensive traveling gave Britton an interest in English antiquities. It also lead to a new interest in architecture. Antiquities and architecture became a part of John Britton's publishing career, dovetailing with his established interest in topography. He authored a large number of books that combined all three, such as The Beauties of England and Wales authored with Brayley and published between 1801 and 1814, Architectural Antiquities of Great Britain and Cathedral Antiquities of England . He edited many more.

Informed by his interest in antiquities, Britton actively campaigned for government protection of monuments in the first half of the nineteenth century. He was also an advisor to the Royal Literary Fund, part of the Art Union Committee, and received a civil-list pension from then Chancellor of the Exchequer Benjamin Disraeli. Britton married Mary Rule (1772-1848) in 1803 and then Ellen Morgan in 1849. No children came from either marriage. John Britton died of bronchitis at his home in St Pancras London on January 1, 1857.

did.unittitle: Series I. Correspondence

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The correspondence series charts Britton's work as an author and as an advocate for the creation of a support network for antiquities in the first half of the 19th century. The latter is especially present in his correspondence with Member of Parliment Joseph Hume, a confidant and supporter of Britton's goals.

did.unittitle: John Britton correspondence wtih Benjamin Strutt and D. Harris

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Letters from Benjamin Strutt, antiquary, concerning St. Botolph's, Colchester; Colcester Castle etc.; 2 letters (undated) concerning the same from D. Harris.

did.unittitle: John Britton correspondence with R.S. Mackenzie, E.W. Brayley, F. Smythies, George Cumberland, and John Goodford

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Letters (1845-05-01) to John Britton from R.S. Mackenzie, concerning Junius and barre (also 1845-02-04). Note and receipt (undated) to John Britton from E.W. Brayley Note (1834-07-10) from John Britton from s. Smythies. George Cumberland to John Britton (1825-02-18) concerning plates, labels, bindings etc. John Goodford of Yeovil to John Britton (1808-12-26) concerning Montacute House for 'Architectural Antiquities.'

did.unittitle: Robert Roberts, Edward Roberts, George Cooke, M. Miller, Edward Goodhall, William Freeman, and H.Law letters to John Britton

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Robert Roberts to John Britton: 3 letters (1827-02, 1826, 1826-11-09) concerning financial arrangements concerning engravings. Edward Roberts to John Britton (undated) 2 letters from George Cooke to John Britton (1825-11-24 and 1825-10-20). M. Miller to John Britton (1825-11-08). Edward Goodhall to John Britton (undated). William Freeman to John Britton (1820-04-24). H. Law to John Britton (1825-01-17).

did.unittitle: Thomas Cubitt and J.C. Still letters to John Britton

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Letter to John Britton to Thomas Cubitt, builder. 1822-08-25 and 1822-11-25; letters from John Britton to J.C. Still, landsteward.

did.unittitle: John Britton correspondence with George Cattermole and H.W. Ball

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Accounts (1823-03-15 to 27) between John Britton and George Cattermole concerning Wells Cathedral, 1843-09-30 letter from John Britton to H.W. Ball concerning Wells Cathedral.

did.unittitle: George Cattermole letters to John Britton and to unidentified

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Two letters from George Cattermole (1823-11-04) and draft reply "after your last insulting letter…I must certainly decline any further personal intercourse, with a man who has done so much ton injure John Britton," (sent 'by Mr. Porden's Pupil); quarrel over non-payment of 6/7 pounds by John Britton to George Cattermole for plate of Covent Garden, which had to be altered to satisfy its architect, Robert Smirke.

did.unittitle: Benjamin Hobhouse letter to Joseph Snow

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Benjamin Hobhouse of Berkeley Square to Joseph Snow concerning the Literary Fund.

did.unittitle: Joseph Hume MP letters to John Britton

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Letters (1839-02-03, 1839-03-28, 1839-10-05, 1839-05-24) from Joseph Hume MP to John Britton who had supplied Hume with books and a report on British Antiquities (for comparison with a report recently produced in France) and correspondence with Lord Lansdown; prior to Hume's approach to Lord Melbourne in 1840 concerning the preservation of British Antiquities.

did.unittitle: John Britton correspondence with Salvandy

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: John Britton invited (1839-02-28) by Salvandy to become Corresponding Member of the Committee on Arts and Monuments set up by the French Ministry of Public Instruction. John Britton replies (1839-10) accepting invitation, despite "having passed my 68th year, (having) employed my head and eyes in literary labours, and the arts, for more than 40"; and even though "I am desirous of relaxing a little from the exertions of reading and writing."

did.unittitle: Joseph Hume MP letter to John Britton

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Hume congratulates John Britton on receipt of medal from King of Prussia and indicates that he will re-submit his proposals concerning British Antiquities (and John Britton's reports), this time to Sir Robert Peel. Also sends John Britton some information about Department of Woods and Forests, on the history of which John Britton is working.

did.unittitle: Joseph Hume MP letter [to John Britton?]

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Joseph Hume sends a contribution to the Britton Testimonial. "I had, long ago, expressed my sense of your claims to public attention by proposing that you should be employed by the Govt. to go round the Kingdom, and place on record your opinion of all the Monuments and Buildings which your labours had not comprehended, with the view of measures being taken to preserve those that should be considered valuable. You are aware that I brought this subject before Parliament, and names you as the man who, of all persons I knew, could and would do justice to…such a commission; and I shall always regret that the Govt. did not adopt my suggestions."

did.unittitle: John Britton letter to Thomas Wyse MP

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: John Britton to Thomas Wyse MP concerning latter's scheme for a "Museum of National Antiquities and Historical Library." John Britton offers his own library of topographical and historical books, mss, etc. (e.g., collections of Stukekley, Carter and William Aleander, ex-keeper of the BM Print Room) as nucleus of new national collection

did.unittitle: Joseph Hume MP letter to John Britton with returned proofs

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Hume returns proofs (1850-02-05) of John Britton's autobiography and recalls the lost opportunity of 1840 – his scheme for a survey and preservation of British Antiquities; enclosure of printed copy of a speech on Parliamentary Reform.

did.unittitle: Joseph Hume MP letters to John Britton?

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Hume to support John Britton's application for a pension from "the Queen's Annual grant" by writing to Lord John Russell. 1851-06-16: Hume to John Britton – still no response from Russell

did.unittitle: John Britton letter draft to Joseph Hume MP

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Draft of letter by John Britton to Hume begging him to use his influence to obtain a civil list pension.

did.unittitle: Rev. Mr. Scarth letter to Rev. Mr. Kilvert

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Concerns Somsert Architectural Society.

did.unittitle: Series II. Printed material

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The printed materials vary in scope and include iterations of Britton's autobiography, obituaries for Joseph Hume, testimonials, and proposals for bills and committees relevant to Britton's work.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Memoir and portrait of John Britton; printed extracts from European Magazine and London Review

did.unittitle: Autobiography of John Britton (presentation copy)

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Presentation copy of John Britton's "Brief Memoir" reprinted from the 'Beauties of Wiltshire' (1825) with letter from John Britton to the Earl of Essex.

did.unittitle: Bill for the Establishment of Schools...proposal by Joseph Hume MP
Suggestions of the National Collection of Studies of our national architecture by E.B. Lamb

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Pamphlet by E.B. Lamb: "Suggestions for a National Collection of Studies of our National Architecture" for "Gothic Architecture has not had its due share of accommodation in the National Museum." This suggestion (1842-07-11) for a collection of Gothic remains at the British Museum was rejected by the Trustees (1842-11-18). Therefore now addressed to the house; Gothic fragments and measured drawings more useful than Greek, yet British Museum is still making space for packing cases of marble fragments. Yet "in our practice of Grecian Architecture we have not got a single step beyond the examples provided by Stuart and his contemporaries, notwithstanding so much – or rather so many things have since been discovered."

Printed appeal on behalf of author James Carter with additional notes

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Printed appeal by John Britton on behalf of a distressed author, James Carter. Quotation on the subject of patronage.

arrangement.p: Material is arranged alphabetically by name of publication, then chronologically.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Material in the publication series connects directly to the many works written by Britton over the years and includes notes about specific topics and extended research and publishing correspondence.
